target_definition: First published reported quarterly PAT attributable to owners, including any eventual exceptional items. No new exceptional item is assumed in these forecasts.
normalization_basis: No exceptional item in any of the four modeled quarters. The large property gain shown in the prior result belongs to December 2024, not December 2025. The company describes December 2025 labour-code impact as immaterial without a separate amount, so no invented addback.

model_formula: (revenue_cr * ebit_margin + other_income_cr - finance_cost_cr + exceptional_pretax_cr) * (1 - tax_rate) + associates_after_tax_cr - nci_cr
margin_definition: EBIT excluding other income and finance costs, after depreciation and amortisation. This is not EBITDA margin.
rationale: Assume partial recovery in commercial CMS shipment timing after a weak Q2 while retaining input-cost and operating-cost pressure. The base is below the H1 average revenue and owner PAT. A single prior December decline is too little evidence for fixed seasonality in a project-driven CDMO. Conversely, an immediate return to the unusually strong Q1 is also unsupported.

parameter_assumptions.revenue: 530 cr, below H1 average 545.617 cr and between the two observed quarters. The recovery is attributed to established commercial molecules, not new clinical successes.
parameter_assumptions.ebit_margin: 22%, between Q2 approximately 15.30% and Q1 approximately 30.60%, below H1 blended 24.30%. More shipment throughput partly absorbs fixed costs while input/freight pressure persists.
parameter_assumptions.other_income: 7.5 cr near Q2. No return from acquired Kakinada land assumed.
parameter_assumptions.finance_cost: 8 cr versus Q2 7.3073 cr, allowing financing and commissioning costs.
parameter_assumptions.tax_rate: 25.3%, close to current H1 effective rate.
parameter_assumptions.nci_cr: Zero. The signed statement identifies both included subsidiaries as wholly owned.

adverse.assumptions: Shipments remain deferred, input/freight pressures persist and fixed-cost absorption weakens. 440 cr revenue and 14% EBIT margin.

base.assumptions: Partial recovery in existing commercial CMS shipments, with earnings below the H1 average.

favorable.assumptions: Larger established commercial shipments return within the quarter. 620 cr revenue and 28% EBIT margin, still below Q1 revenue and margin.

scenario_interpretation: Uncalibrated operating sensitivities. No probabilities, confidence interval, or claim these exhaust possible outcomes.
unknowns: Shipment timing, commercial-molecule customer concentration and product mix are not disclosed at the resolution needed for a December schedule.
RFPs and early clinical projects do not equal near-term revenue. No specific approvals or new commercial launches are assumed.
Geopolitical input/freight costs, new R&D staffing and depreciation may offset higher throughput.
Management commentary uses standalone headlines. All model financial anchors are from the consolidated signed results.
scope_of_review: Quarterly forecasting supplement. No complete governance, valuation, management-quality, liquidity or portfolio suitability review. No new investment verdict.

issuer_claims.claim: Management says H1 was broadly in line with its plan and annual growth expectations remain intact. Commercial CMS shipments can move between quarters.
Peptide capability, new R&D facilities and Kakinada land are long-term investments. Kakinada should not be treated as an immediate-return asset.

baseline_correction.reason: Signed consolidated PAT and wholly owned subsidiary note override inconsistent imported owner fields. PBT less tax reconciles to the signed numbers.
